articles.title: Here's Everything You Need to Know About Mighty Mike Plays and the $118,000 He Allegedly Cost His Dad
articles.summary: Why is everyone talking about Mighty Mike Plays? From the (alleged) $118,000 bill to AI-generated T-shirt designs, we're here to explain how a Minecraft YouTube channel has captured the internet's attention.
body: It's a tale as old as time: a child is playing a video game, they grab their parent's credit card, and all of a sudden, someone has a thousand-dollar hole in their bank account. The story of Mighty Mike has so much in common with the lesson countless others have learned in the past – or does it?
Over the space of just a week, a nine-year-old YouTuber and his dad have ensnared an audience of millions, but not everyone is buying the events that started with a 14-minute Minecraft upload.

It's a sweet story that, apparently, as of September 14, started to come to an end. With a half-hearted "wassup chat" and a title that read " Message from Dad…Mighty Mike Plays is Over," it was clear the video lacked the same enthusiasm present in previous uploads. The channel's nine-year-old owner quickly signaled that the page would soon be shut down before handing the mic over to his dad, Dave, for an explanation.
points: Why is everyone talking about Mighty Mike Plays?

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall Review
articles.summary: Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm.
body: Things only get more alarming from there, but Townfall dragged me through its increasingly squeamish scenes with the powerful allure of its central mystery, which gradually brings to light the tragic events that have impacted the town, the main players at fault, and exactly where poor Simon stands in all of it. It’s a story that deals with familiar themes of trauma and guilt that we’ve come to expect from Silent Hill, but it also tackles previously unexplored shades of evil like corporate greed and environmental mismanagement that help to make it feel like a refreshingly new twist on the series’ formula.

Although he comes across as fairly monotone at first, I grew to appreciate the understated earnestness of Simon as the events of Townfall mine the full depths of his despair, especially compared to some of the overly dramatic heroes of the earlier Silent Hill games. At certain junctions, the story also switches the perspective to a couple of other playable characters that further flesh out the details of what’s really going on, but I’d rather not spoil exactly who they are other than to say that they provide crucial roles in unravelling St. Amelia’s secrets.
points: Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm.

articles.title: 'Sherlock Holmes Meets NCIS' Hit 2000s Detective Series Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: The age of the great American cop show is over. Yes, franchises like NCIS and Law & Order are likely to continue until the heat death of the universe, but network TV used to be packed full of idiosyncratic crime-solvers, usually but not necessarily working hand-in-hand with local law enforcement.
body: Elementary is a modernization of the Sherlock Holmes story, which sets it in present-day New York City. When the show begins, Holmes (Jonny Lee Miller) is newly sober, following a stint in rehab for narcotics addiction, and has relocated from London to Manhattan.

Holmes' father, without consulting him, hires Dr. Joan Watson (Lucy Liu) to live with him as his "sober companion." Watson, a former surgeon turned addiction specialist, gets dragged along for the ride as Holmes pursues his only real passion: solving murders as a consultant for the NYPD.

Watching Elementary for the first time in 2026, it's one of the more entertaining depictions of Holmes. Miller plays him as brilliant but unfocused, and he’s consistently on thin ice with every person around him in one way or another. It's a far cry from the mellower Holmes of Arthur Conan Doyle's stories, but Miller's version is newly sober and recently traumatized. If you give it a few episodes, it does eventually make sense that Elementary 's Holmes is one big raw nerve.
points: The age of the great American cop show is over.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine "fart gas" scent trails addressed by a surprise update
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine has received a hotfix update that addresses one of the core features in the game many people have an issue with: scent trails. These are represented on screen by a gassy, bright blue line, and they're used by Wolverine to locate his next mission objective and to find collectibles…
body: This patch, version 01.001.005, doesn't remove the scent trails but it does change their opacity so they're less pronounced. The same also extends to audio sense indicators, toning them down.

In the blog post announcing the hotfix, developer Insomniac Games said it "continues to evaluate ways to further improve senses", and that it's exploring offering the ability to toggle them off entirely in a future update.

Dubbed "fart gas" by some players, the feature has been widely mocked online. Even before the game's launch, fans asked for a toggle to turn it off once it became clear they found the scents distracting.
Insomniac has also addressed some game crashes, which apparently "a small percentage of players" were experiencing.

articles.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 6 Review & Recap
articles.summary: Lanterns stumbles in Episode 6, as the series finally returns to the present day but struggles to maintain its narrative momentum. Read our full review.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 6!

It was obvious from watching Lanterns Episode 5 that the series was due for a major shake-up in the remaining three installments. The 2016 storyline reached its fiery climax, as half of Rushville was destroyed, the Manhunter stood revealed, and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) finally had their big falling-out. The series now pivots by returning fully to the 2026 timeline first teased in the pilot and digging into the mystery surrounding Hal's apparent murder. Lanterns is a very different show in Episode 6, and not necessarily for the better.

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall Is Genuinely Scary, Then Gets Really Dull | Review
articles.summary: The most straightforward answer is that these are psychological horror games which are about something: unforgivable crimes, abusive childhoods, systemic misogyny. Compared to its peers, Silent Hill has always stood out for its heavy themes and persistent symbolism, with every monster carrying a…
body: What exactly defines the Silent Hill series? Is it an unassuming town blanketed in fog, a place where horrors are hidden just out of sight? Is it the survival gameplay and cryptic puzzles? Or is it the sound of an air raid siren, and Pyramid Head dragging his bloody cleaver across concrete?

The latest entry in the series, Silent Hill: Townfall, hits all these points. Its setting, a Scottish fishing village, is so evocative that you can practically smell the sea salt. Its creatures double as metaphors, with scares that carry deeper meaning. And of course, there’s the fog, rolling in off the ocean to hide horrible deeds.

articles.title: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story Review
articles.summary: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story aims to be an insightful commentary on female rage, but it never commits to how it wants to convey that message.
body: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story is now streaming on Netflix. This review contains spoilers.

“Sometimes I wonder did she really do these things? Or is it just a story with embellishments? Could people really be that cruel back then?” Lizzie Borden (Ella Beatty) asks this of her housemaid/lover Bridget "Maggie" Sullivan ( Vicky Krieps ) as they read about Countess Elizabeth Báthory. It’s just one of the many on-the-nose moments in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, the fourth installment in Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s true crime Netflix franchise.

This season explores the 1892 murders of wealthy Andrew Borden (Charlie Hunnam) and his wife Abby (Rebecca Hall) in Fall River, Massachusetts. Andrew’s youngest daughter Lizzie is tried for their murders but acquitted by an all-male jury thanks largely to shoddy police work and the belief that a woman was incapable of committing such a heinous, violent crime. Those are the basic facts of the Borden case.
points: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story aims to be an insightful commentary on female rage, but it never commits to how it wants to convey that message.

Three years later, Abrams’ paranormal sci-fi series, Fringe, opened with a similar aerial disaster. Although the plane in question doesn’t crash, its safe landing through autopilot raises unsettling questions about the state of the passengers found inside.

The reception to Fringe was nowhere near as enthusiastic as Lost, but the show's cultural perception gradually improved over the course of five seasons. And if you’re interested in Abrams’ cult sci-fi series and the convoluted lore it has to offer, now's your chance. You can stream Fringe for free on Pluto TV at no cost whatsoever.

In Fringe, the FBI supports a Joint Federal Task Force known as the Fringe Division, who investigate cases related to speculative science, like parallel universes and technological singularities. The team includes Agent Olivia Dunham (Anna Torv), Dr. Walter Bishop (John Noble), and his estranged son, Peter Bishop (Joshua Jackson).

articles.title: 25 Years Later, the GameCube’s 5 Best Launch Games Are Still As Good as Ever
articles.summary: This week marked the 25th anniversary of the Nintendo GameCube, and boy do I feel old. I still have vivid memories of the GameCube’s North American launch (which came a few months after Japan, in November 2001), because it was the first video game console that was truly mine, rather than one I…
body: To celebrate the GameCube’s anniversary, and to test that my noggin still works, let’s take a walk down memory lane and reminisce about the console’s best launch games. Though the GameCube had several day one games in North America thanks to an influx of sports titles, there were five standouts that were must-own games right out the gate.

Wave Race: Blue Storm is one of those Nintendo launch games that’s easy to underappreciate. A jet ski racing game was certainly less exciting on paper than a totally new franchise starring a beloved Mario character. It was the console’s second banana at the time, but it deserves its flowers in retrospect. It was a rock solid racing game that successfully showed off what was possible on new hardware. Speedy races and impressive water effects make for the kind of GameCube pioneer that you have to respect.

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall review - an often inspired, if slightly lumbering trek into the fog
articles.summary: Once a fictional town in Maine, Silent Hill has broken containment and become a transferable oral history mechanism, offered to videogame developers worldwide as a way of investigating, even celebrating local culture.
body: Townfall is the tale of the fictional late 90s Scottish island community of St Ameila, explored through the intersecting lives of three people. The first of these is Simon, a bespectacled and bemused Black American with a cannula of gritty fluid wrapped around one arm, who hauls himself onto the pier at the start of the game. Simon is here to do something for Richard, a grave and insistent white American who sends instructions by way of a chunky pocket TV that appears capable of two-way communication. Simon is also embroiled in a search for Zoe, a local white English nurse who is carrying a world of hurt on her shoulders.

articles.title: Call of Duty maker Activision claims video game cheating is now a £6.3 billion ($8.5 billion) a year industry
articles.summary: Activision has published a breakdown of the numbers behind cheating in its games, claiming cheating is big business, generating about £6.3 billion - $8.5bn - every year in account sales, boosting, and spoofing services.
body: In a blog posted on the publisher's website, the publisher's cheat squad, Team Ricochet, said cheat subscriptions across 15 games alone generate around £2.6 billion ($3.5 billion).

Activision said it has "paired technical detection with sustained legal action to destabilise the cheat ecosystem at every level", disrupting more than 375 reseller operations, issuing more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and shutting down 31 primary cheat vendors.

The publisher also claims cheat sellers regularly hide the fact their products have been detected, instead blaming outages on excuses like illness, surgery or car accidents to keep customers on side before admitting their cheats are no longer working.

Activision says the crackdown is also driving up costs for cheaters themselves, with subscriptions costing upwards of £75 ($100), spoofing tools adding further recurring fees, and some players spending more than £750 ($1,000) a year in total.

articles.title: First 5-day Tokyo Game Show in 30 years cuts back to 4 in face of Typhoon Dujuan
articles.summary: As reported by Kotaku, the organizers of the Tokyo Game Show have announced that its final day has been canceled and tickets for Monday, September 21 will be refunded.
body: "Due to the approach of Typhoon No. 25, strong winds and rain are expected to intensify in the afternoon and beyond, and disruptions to transportation are also a concern," event organizers wrote on Twitter. "Therefore, prioritizing the safety of all attendees, exhibitors, and related parties, as well as ensuring safe return home, we have decided to cancel the event for the entire day."
The TGS showfloor will remain open for today, September 20, with potential modifications. There is no word on how the event will address publishers and devs who rented out space for the final day.

As reported by the Japan Times, Dujuan is the 25th named typhoon of 2026, and is predicted to dump the heaviest rainfall (almost 16 inches) on the Kanto region containing Tokyo. Nippon Airways has canceled many flights in the region, while the East Japan Railway is fully and partially suspending service on some lines.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima responds to accusations of Physint being over budget and late on deadline, says he still "loves Sony" despite collapse of publishing deal
articles.summary: Last week, we learned that Sony "stepped away" from Kojima Production's previously PlayStation-exclusive "action espionage" game Physint. Following the announcement, which saw Xbox take over publishing duties for the in-development title, a new report has claimed Sony's decision was the result of…
body: Now, IGN has conducted an interview with Kojima that sheds a little more light on the situation. In the chat - which covers a range of topics including Kojima's fears for the future of the studio, the perils of working on multiple projects at once, and the implications of losing Sony resources - Kojima detailed how the conversation with the platform holder went, noting how that he was in a state of shock at the time, and finds the meeting difficult to recall.

"I don't remember so much of that meeting, to be honest with you," Kojima told IGN. "And my colleagues probably don't remember as well, so I can't really answer if you ask me what exactly they said. But, from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry.

"Nothing could've prepared me for their decision to step away from the project. So I thought, "What am I going to do from tomorrow?" But from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry."
